newsitem.title: FINLAND: POHJOLA CEO EXPECTS SALAMA DEAL APPROVAL.
newsitem.headline: POHJOLA CEO EXPECTS SALAMA DEAL APPROVAL.

text.p: Finnish insurance group Vakuutusosakeyhtio Pohjola's CEO Iiro Viinanen said on Tuesday he expected mutual life assurance firm Suomi's representatives assembly to approve the sale of Suomi's Salama unit to Pohjola.
"It would be quite a surprise if it were not approved," Viinanen told Reuters. The assembly will meet on May 6.

Earlier, Suomi's supervisory board approved the plan. The board decided to sell Suomi's 92 percent stake in Salama to Pohjola for 537.3 million markka, and give up underwriting new business for a compensation of 54 million markka, Suomi said in a statement.

Viinanen said he expected that the authorities -- the insurance supervision at the ministry of social affairs and health -- would also approve the planned restructuring of Pohjola and Suomi "in due course".

The life insurance market was in for "strong growth" for many years to come, Viinanen said. He said he expected total domestic life insurance premium income to increase "perhaps three-fold" in the next 10 years. --Helsinki newsroom +358-9-680 50 245, e-mail news@reuters.fi
